n75e1efaea0a.s: Which type of Bill may require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures?
o: Constitution Amendment Bill affecting federal provisions
n75e1efaea0a.x: Constitution Amendment Bills affecting specified federal provisions need ratification by at least half the States; ordinary Bills need only a simple majority in Parliament.

n3ab00ee926b.s: What is the role of State Legislatures in amending the Constitution under Article 368?
o: They can initiate an amendment by resolution
They can introduce amendment Bills in Parliament on State subjects
They can refer amendment Bills to the Supreme Court
They can only ratify certain amendment Bills passed by Parliament
n3ab00ee926b.x: States cannot initiate amendments under Article 368; they only ratify amendments to specified federal provisions.

nd7ff850e660.s: How is a deadlock between the two Houses on a Constitution Amendment Bill resolved?
o: By a joint sitting under Article 108
There is no mechanism: a joint sitting is not available
By ratification of half the States
By reference to the Supreme Court
nd7ff850e660.x: The Constitution provides no joint sitting for amendment Bills, so a deadlock cannot be resolved; this absence is itself a criticism of the procedure.

nfe7f719f672.s: Ratification by the States is required for:
o: Only a limited group of federal provisions
Only amendments passed by a joint sitting
nfe7f719f672.x: State ratification is needed only for a limited group of federal provisions, not for every amendment.

n21205b63515.s: By what majority does a State Legislature ratify a Constitution Amendment Bill?
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
Majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting
n21205b63515.x: Ratification is by a simple majority of each concerned State Legislature, and no time limit is prescribed for it.

nb607dccdae5.s: Once a Constitution Amendment Bill is duly passed, the President:
o: May withhold assent in the public interest
May return it once for reconsideration
May refer it to a joint sitting
nb607dccdae5.x: Assent to a duly passed amendment Bill is obligatory: the President can neither withhold it nor return the Bill (24th Amendment, 1971).

n86010077b43.s: Which Amendment inserted clauses (4) and (5) in Article 368 to bar judicial review of constitutional amendments?
n86010077b43.x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 inserted Article 368(4) and (5) to declare the amending power unlimited and bar judicial review of amendments.

nindian-polity-24-5.s: Which case held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights?
nindian-polity-24-5.x: Golaknath held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights; Sajjan Singh had earlier upheld that power.

nindian-polity-24-37.s: What did Kesavananda Bharati (1973) hold about Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights?
o: Parliament cannot amend them at all
Parliament can amend them only with State ratification
Parliament can amend them only by a joint sitting
Parliament can amend them but not destroy the basic structure
nindian-polity-24-37.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973, 13 judges) held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot destroy the Constitution's basic structure.

nindian-polity-67-14.s: By what majority was the 13-Judge Bench in Kesavananda Bharati divided?
nindian-polity-67-14.x: Kesavananda Bharati was decided by a 13-Judge Bench by a 7:6 majority.

n3feb16e2d69.s: An amendment Bill got 298 votes for and 230 against, with 528 present and voting. How many 'yes' votes did two-thirds need?
n3feb16e2d69.x: Two-thirds of 528 is 352; with only 298 votes in favour the Bill failed the two-thirds requirement.

n95ee5016224.s: On which date did President Rajendra Prasad give assent to the First Amendment?
n95ee5016224.x: The First Amendment, enacted by the Provisional Parliament under PM Nehru, received assent on 18 June 1951.

n17bc40348dc.s: Which word in the Preamble was NOT added by the 42nd Amendment?
n17bc40348dc.x: The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'; 'Justice' was already in the original Preamble.

n07a36cd13b2.s: After the 44th Amendment, the right to property is a legal right under:
n07a36cd13b2.x: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and kept property as a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

nd4e7dddef78.s: After the 44th Amendment, rights under which Articles cannot be suspended during a National Emergency?
nd4e7dddef78.x: The 44th Amendment provides that Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.

n81e06c36839.s: Part IXA relating to municipalities was added by which Amendment?
n81e06c36839.x: Part IXA on municipalities came with the 74th Amendment; the 73rd added Part IX (Panchayats) and the Eleventh Schedule.

nindian-polity-22-12.s: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze of seat allocation on the 1971 Census up to:
nindian-polity-22-12.x: The 84th Amendment froze seat allocation on the 1971 Census until 2026, not 2030.

nindian-polity-23-13.s: Article 15(5), enabling OBC reservation in educational institutions, was inserted by which Amendment?
nindian-polity-23-13.x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) added Article 15(5); the 86th (2002) added Article 21A.

nindian-polity-23-40.s: Which Amendment barred defectors from becoming Ministers?
nindian-polity-23-40.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) barred defectors from becoming Ministers; the 52nd (1985) had introduced anti-defection disqualification.

nindian-polity-43-30.x: The 104th ended Anglo-Indian nominations; EWS came with the 103rd, GST with the 101st and women's reservation with the 106th.

n8ba00c33e95.s: Which Amendment raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62?
n8ba00c33e95.x: The 15th Amendment (1963) raised the HC judges' retirement age from 60 to 62; the 12th (1962) made Goa, Daman and Diu a Union Territory.

n00460378936.s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was provided for by which Amendment?
n00460378936.x: The 99th Amendment, 2014 provided for the NJAC, struck down in 2015; the 97th, 100th and 102nd dealt with co-operatives, the Land Boundary Agreement and the NCBC.

nb6453fb1f6a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2025?
o: It concerns removal of the PM, CMs and Ministers detained for 30 consecutive days on serious charges
It increases the Lok Sabha strength to 850 members
nb6453fb1f6a.x: Raising the Lok Sabha to 850 was the 131st Bill; the 130th concerns removal of Ministers detained for 30 consecutive days and amends Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.

new.s: Besides the 24th Amendment, which Amendment amended Article 368 itself?
new.x: Article 368 was amended by the 24th (1971) and the 101st (2016) Amendments.

new.s: Which Article on joint sittings does NOT apply to Constitution Amendment Bills?
new.x: Article 108 (joint sitting) does not apply to amendment Bills, so each House must pass them separately.

new.s: Amendment of the Directive Principles of State Policy requires:
o: Special majority plus ratification by half the States
new.x: DPSPs, like Fundamental Rights, are amended by special majority without State ratification.

new.s: Laws under Articles 2-4 and 169 are passed by simple majority of members:
o: Of the total membership of each House
Present and voting, and are not deemed amendments under Article 368
Present and voting in the Rajya Sabha only
Of both Houses at a joint sitting, with State ratification
new.x: Simple-majority changes are by members present and voting and are not deemed amendments under Article 368.

new.s: Which of the following does NOT require ratification by the States?
new.x: The election of the President needs ratification, but his qualifications, conditions of office and tenure do not.

new.s: A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249 to let Parliament legislate on a State List subject needs:
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha
Majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting in each House
Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
Simple majority of the Rajya Sabha
new.x: Articles 249 and 312 need two-thirds of members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha only.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 61 – two-thirds of members present and voting in each House
Article 249 – two-thirds of total membership of the Lok Sabha
Article 312 – two-thirds present and voting in the Rajya Sabha only
Removal of the CAG – simple majority
new.x: Article 312 (new All-India Services) needs two-thirds present and voting in the Rajya Sabha; Article 61 needs two-thirds of total membership; CAG removal needs the Article 368 type.

new.s: Unlike some constitutions, India's amendment procedure has no special body (convention) and no:
new.x: Critics note there is no special body or referendum for amendments; special majority, assent and State ratification all exist.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about criticism of the amendment procedure:
1. There is no time limit within which States must ratify an amendment.
2. State Legislatures may initiate amendments on federal provisions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is a recognised criticism. Statement 2 is wrong: States cannot initiate amendments at all.

new.s: Which change made by the 42nd Amendment was later undone?
o: Six-year term of the Lok Sabha
new.x: The 44th Amendment restored the five-year term; the Preamble words and Fundamental Duties remain.

new.s: Which Directive Principles were newly inserted by the 42nd Amendment?
new.x: The 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A and 43A (also 39(f) and 48A) to the DPSPs.

new.s: The 44th Amendment was enacted by the Janata government of which Prime Minister?
new.x: The Janata government under PM Morarji Desai enacted the 44th Amendment as a corrective to the 38th, 39th and 42nd.

new.s: The 89th Amendment, 2003 provided for:
o: Separate NCSC and NCST under Articles 338 and 338A
Ministers limited to 15% of the House
new.x: The 89th split the commission into the NCSC and NCST (338, 338A); the 15% limit was the 91st and Delhi NCT the 69th.

new.s: Reservation in promotions for SCs and STs under Article 16(4A) was introduced by which Amendment?
new.x: The 77th Amendment (1995) inserted Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotions.

new.s: 'Consequential seniority' for SCs/STs in promotions was provided by which Amendment?
new.x: The 85th Amendment (2001) added consequential seniority to 16(4A), retrospective from 17 June 1995.

new.s: The 82nd Amendment allowed relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion through a proviso to:
new.x: The 82nd Amendment (2000) added a proviso to Article 335; Article 16(4B) was the 81st.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 81st Amendment – carry forward of unfilled vacancies outside the 50% ceiling
new.x: The 81st inserted 16(4B) on carry-forward vacancies; consequential seniority was the 85th, 16(4A) the 77th, and the 62nd extended SC/ST seats.

new.s: The 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Amendments were all upheld in which case?
new.x: All four SC/ST reservation amendments were upheld in M. Nagaraj (2006).

new.s: Article 371E, inserted by the 32nd Amendment, provides for:
o: A Central University in Andhra Pradesh
new.x: Article 371E provides for a Central University in AP; the Six-Point Formula is Article 371D.

new.s: Articles 371D and 371E were extended to Telangana by:
new.x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Articles 371D and 371E to Telangana.

new.s: Which Article inserted by the 106th Amendment reserves seats for women in State Legislative Assemblies?
new.x: Article 332A covers State Assemblies; 330A covers the Lok Sabha and 334A the timing.

new.s: For how many years does women's reservation under the 106th Amendment last, unless extended by Parliament?
new.x: It lasts 15 years from commencement, extendable by Parliament by law.

new.s: Under Article 243ZJ, the maximum number of directors on a co-operative board is:
new.x: The 97th Amendment's Article 243ZJ caps the board at 21 directors, not 31.

new.s: The 103rd Amendment was passed as which Constitution Amendment Bill?
new.x: The EWS amendment was passed as the 124th Amendment Bill, 2019.

new.s: By what majority did the Supreme Court uphold the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan (2022)?
new.x: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (7 Nov 2022) upheld the EWS amendment by 3:2.

new.s: Which Article inserted by the 101st Amendment created the GST Council?
new.x: Article 279A created the GST Council; 246A gives concurrent GST power and 269A covers inter-State supply.

new.s: Nagaland became a State through which Amendment, which also inserted Article 371A?
new.x: The 13th Amendment (1962) made Nagaland a State with Article 371A.

new.s: Arunachal Pradesh became a State with Article 371H through which Amendment?
new.x: The 55th Amendment (1986) is Arunachal Pradesh; the 53rd is Mizoram and the 56th Goa.

new.s: The 100th Amendment implemented the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement covering how many Indian enclaves?
new.x: The 100th Amendment (2015) covered 111 Indian and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves.

new.s: Under the 97th Amendment, a co-operative board must reserve seats for:
o: Two SC/ST members and one woman
One SC/ST member and two women
new.x: Co-operative boards reserve one seat for SC/ST and two for women, with a 5-year term.

new.s: Which Article was omitted by the 101st Amendment?
new.x: The 101st omitted Article 268A (service tax) and inserted 246A, 269A and 279A.

new.s: Article 246A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, provides for:
o: Power of both Parliament and States to make GST laws
new.x: 246A lets Parliament and the States both make GST laws; 269A is inter-State supply and 279A the GST Council.

new.s: The GST Council takes decisions by a majority of:
new.x: The GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, decides by a three-fourths majority.

new.s: Which Article, inserted by the 102nd Amendment, gave constitutional status to the NCBC?
new.x: Article 338B made the NCBC constitutional; 342A lets the President notify the SEBC list.

new.s: The 105th Amendment restored the States' power to identify their own SEBCs through:
new.x: The 105th inserted 342A(3), letting States/UTs identify their own SEBCs.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 102nd and 105th Amendments:
1. The 102nd Amendment received assent on 11 August 2018.
2. The 105th Amendment took away the States' power to identify SEBCs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 105th restored the States' power to identify SEBCs.

new.s: Which clauses did the 103rd Amendment insert for EWS reservation?
new.x: The 103rd inserted 15(6) for education and 16(6) for jobs, up to 10% for EWS.

new.s: The 103rd Amendment received Presidential assent on:
new.x: The 103rd received assent on 12 January 2019; 7 November 2022 is the Janhit Abhiyan judgment.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022):
1. It upheld the 103rd Amendment by a 3:2 majority.
2. It held that the 50% ceiling applies to EWS reservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 50% ceiling applies to 15(4), 15(5) and 16(4), not EWS.

new.s: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation under Article 334 up to:
new.x: The 104th extended SC/ST seat reservation in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies to 2030.

new.s: The nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and Assemblies ended with effect from:
new.x: The 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination, effective January 2020.

new.s: In which year did the 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) receive Presidential assent?
new.x: It received assent on 28 September 2023.

new.s: Seats for women in the Lok Sabha under the 106th Amendment are reserved by:
new.x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha; 332A State Assemblies; 243T is municipal women's reservation.

new.s: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024 on One Nation, One Election inserts Article 82A and amends:
new.x: The 129th Bill amends Articles 83, 172 and 327; 75, 164 and 239AA belong to the 130th Bill.
